reducers()

The reducers() method registers one or more reducer functions on a FeatureCell. Reducers are responsible for deriving the next immutable state snapshot during pipeline execution.

Method Contract Summary

  • Reducers are registered declaratively during FeatureCell initialization
  • Reducers execute after operators and filters
  • Reducers receive the current immutable state snapshot
  • Reducers must return a value of the same structural type
  • Errors during reducer execution propagate as Vault errors

The reducers() method defines state derivation only. Reducers are the only pipeline stage permitted to produce a new state value, but they do not emit snapshots directly, influence pipeline control flow, or perform side effects.

Note

The reducers() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each call appends reducer functions to the FeatureCell’s reducer list. Reducers execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, the recommended practice is to register related reducer functions as a single ordered array to preserve clarity and intentional execution ordering.

reducers()

The reducers() method registers one or more reducer functions that execute during the Reducer stage of the pipeline. Each reducer receives the current immutable state snapshot and returns the next state value.

Example: Registering Reducer Functions

{{`this.vault
  .reducers([
    (current) => ({
      ...current,
      count: current.count + 1
    })
  ])
  .initialize();`}}
 
{{`employeeCell
  .reducers([
    (current) => ({
      ...current,
      count: current.count + 1
    })
  ])
  .initialize();`}}

What this does

  • Registers one or more reducer functions on the FeatureCell
  • Reducers execute during the Reducer stage
  • Each reducer receives the current immutable state snapshot
  • The returned value becomes the next state snapshot

Reducers must be pure, must not mutate the incoming state, and must always return a value of the same structural type.
